question.text: In the primary market, securities can be issued by which of the following parties?

answer.text: Central/State/Local Governments, Public Sector Units, Private Sector Companies, Banks, Financial Institutions, NBFCs and Mutual Funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.1.4 (iv), issuers in the primary market include Central/State/Local Governments, PSUs, Private Sector Companies, Banks, Financial Institutions, NBFCs and Mutual Funds. On SSE specifically, NPOs and FPEs are the issuer classes. The Trap: Options A, C and D artificially narrow the issuer universe. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets Foundation) and XV (Research Analyst) where issuer-side analysis is central. SIAs identify NPO/FPE issuer class when scoping SSE instrument-specific assurance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: On SSE engagements, know whether the issuer is using ZCZP (debt-like), equity (FPE only), or MF-for-SSE units (retail). Each instrument carries different disclosure triggers — your SAS scope must align.
